settings.title: Settings
settings.speechModeAppliesTo: Applies to your voice. Other's audio always uses semantic VAD.
settings.speechModeTooltip:
Auto: the provider detects when you have finished speaking. 
Push-to-Talk: hold Space or the mic button to send audio manually. 
Push-to-Translate: like Push-to-Talk, but routes your raw mic to the virtual mic when idle so you can speak directly without translation.
settings.speechModeAppliesToAuto: Applies to your voice. Other's audio always uses the provider's automatic detection.

noiseSuppressionTooltip.off: Off — Browser's built-in noise handling only.
noiseSuppressionTooltip.standard: Standard (RNNoise) — Lightweight AI noise suppression with low latency.
noiseSuppressionTooltip.enhanced: Enhanced (GTCRN) — High-quality AI noise suppression, best for complex noise environments.

echoCancellationTooltip.app: Sokuji only — Removes Sokuji's translated speech if the microphone picks it up. Choose this when the microphone is a virtual cable such as BlackHole.
echoCancellationTooltip.browser: Browser only — Removes what this browser plays, meeting tabs included, if the microphone picks it up. Choose this when the microphone is a virtual cable such as BlackHole carrying another app's sound.
echoCancellationTooltip.all: All sounds — Also removes what other apps play through the speakers, such as a meeting app. A virtual cable used as the microphone carries exactly that sound, so it would go silent.

settings.regionNotSupported: Service not available in your region. Please check your network environment or try a different provider.
settings.sessionActiveNotice: Settings are locked while session is active. Please end the session to modify settings.
settings.volcengineAST2InfoText: Doubao AST 2.0 provides speech-to-speech simultaneous interpretation. The translation can be spoken in the speaker's own cloned voice, or in a voice picked from its voice library.
settings.volcengineAST2TurnDetectionTooltip:
Auto: server-side voice activity detection. 
Push-to-Talk: hold Space or the mic button to send audio manually. 
Push-to-Translate: like Push-to-Talk, but routes your raw mic to the virtual mic when idle so you can speak directly without translation.
settings.volcengineAST2ReplacementLibraryTooltip: Post-transcription regex text substitution. The referenced library must be a regex word list, not a standard replacement list.
settings.volcengineAST2CustomVocabularyFooter: Invalid or empty library IDs are silently ignored — the session runs as if the field weren't set. Library changes made in the Volcengine console can take a few minutes to take effect.
settings.geminiParticipantTokenWarning: Gemini generates audio responses for Other's audio that are discarded, resulting in additional token usage.
settings.diagnosticLogsTooltip: Record what the app does, so you can attach it to a bug report. Off by default. While on, a “Logs” button appears in the title bar, and the setting stays on after a restart.
settings.appearanceTooltip: How the app looks. System follows the operating system's light or dark setting.
settings.helpDiscussionsTooltip: Feature requests, feedback, and community discussions
settings.providerTooltip: Choose your AI translation service. Each service has different features, voices, and pricing. OpenAI offers the most features, while Gemini provides a good free tier. Local (Offline) mode is completely free — no API key or internet required.
settings.modelTooltip: The AI model affects speed and quality. 'Mini' models are faster but simpler. Standard models are more accurate but slightly slower. Try mini first for cost efficiency.
settings.voiceTooltip: Choose the AI's speaking voice. Each voice has different tone and style. Try different ones to find your favorite.
settings.voicePreviewNeedsKey: Save your API key to preview voices.
settings.geminiVoicePreviewNote: Previewing a voice synthesizes one short sentence with your Gemini API key, which Google may bill.
settings.turnDetectionTooltip:
How AI knows when you've finished speaking. 
Normal: Waits for silence. 
Semantic: AI understands context. 
Push-to-Talk: Manual control. 
Push-to-Translate: Manual control with raw mic passthrough to the virtual mic when idle.
settings.thresholdTooltip: Voice detection sensitivity (0.0-1.0). Lower values detect quieter sounds but may trigger accidentally. Higher values need louder speech. Default 0.5 works for most.
settings.prefixPaddingTooltip: Silent time to keep before your speech starts (seconds). Helps capture the beginning of sentences. Too high delays response. Try 0.3-0.5.
settings.silenceDurationTooltip: How long to wait after you stop talking (seconds). Short = quick response but might cut you off. Long = waits patiently but slower. Try 0.5.
settings.semanticEagernessTooltip:
How quickly AI decides you're done (Semantic mode only). 
Auto: AI decides. 
Low: Very patient. 
Medium: Balanced. 
High: Quick to respond.
settings.temperatureTooltip: Translation creativity (0.0-1.0). Lower = more literal, word-for-word translation. Higher = more natural, conversational style. For translation, 0.7-0.9 works best.
settings.maxTokensTooltip: Maximum length of each translation. Tokens are like word pieces - 100 tokens ≈ 75 words. 2048-4096 good for conversations. 'inf' = unlimited.
settings.transcriptModelTooltip:
Speech recognition model for your own words. This only affects the original text shown next to each translation — the translation itself is produced from your audio directly. 
gpt-live-transcribe: Most accurate, streams as you speak, and the priciest. 
gpt-transcribe: Current generation, transcribes each finished turn. 
gpt-4o-mini-transcribe: Cheapest, the default. 
gpt-4o-transcribe / whisper-1: Older models.
settings.transcriptKeywordsTooltip: Names, jargon, and product terms the transcriber should be ready for, separated by commas. Hints only — a term appears in the transcript only when it is actually spoken. Supported by gpt-live-transcribe and gpt-transcribe.
settings.noiseReductionTooltip:
Background noise removal. 
None: No processing, use in quiet rooms. 
Near field: For headsets/close microphones. 
Far field: For speakers/conference rooms with echo.
settings.systemInstructionsTooltip: Custom instructions for the AI translator. Tell it your preferences like formal/casual tone, technical terms handling, or specific translation style.
settings.participantInstructionsTooltip:
System instructions for translating Other's audio. If empty, the main instructions above will be used.

Important: Your main instructions may have the wrong language direction for the other side. Example: If you speak Chinese and your main instructions translate Chinese→Japanese, but the other side speaks Japanese, the main instructions would incorrectly try to translate Japanese→Japanese. Set separate Other's instructions to translate Japanese→Chinese.
settings.localTranslationPromptTooltip: Customize how the local translation model is instructed. Only applies to Qwen-family models.
settings.localPromptUnsupported: Current translation model does not support custom prompts. Switch to a Qwen-family model in Model Management to enable.
settings.localPromptNoThinkHint: For Qwen3 models, ` /no_think` will be automatically appended.
settings.participantInstructionsPlaceholder: Leave empty to use main instructions
settings.localInferenceTurnDetectionTooltip:
Auto: local Voice Activity Detection automatically detects speech. 
Push-to-Talk: hold Space or the mic button to send audio manually. 
Push-to-Translate: like Push-to-Talk, but routes your raw mic to the virtual mic when idle so you can speak directly without translation.
settings.vadSettingsTooltip: Voice Activity Detection configuration. Adjust these settings to optimize speech detection for your environment.
settings.vadThresholdTooltip: Speech detection sensitivity. Higher values require louder/clearer speech to trigger recognition. Lower values are more sensitive to quiet speech.
settings.vadNegativeThresholdTooltip: Probability below which silence starts counting toward the end of a segment. Auto keeps it 0.15 under the VAD Threshold. It never applies above the VAD Threshold — that would stop segments from ever ending.
settings.vadMinSilenceDurationTooltip: Minimum silence duration to split speech segments. Shorter values split sentences faster, longer values wait for more natural pauses.
settings.vadMaxSpeechDurationTooltip: Longest a single speech segment can run before it is split. Some models split sooner, at the longest segment they transcribe correctly.
settings.vadPreSpeechPadDurationTooltip: Audio kept from just before speech is detected, so the first sound of a sentence is not cut off. Longer values also pass more of the noise before you speak to recognition.
settings.smartTurnCheckAfterTooltip: How long a pause lasts before Smart Turn checks whether you have finished speaking. If you have, the segment ends at once instead of waiting for Max Wait.
settings.smartTurnThresholdTooltip: How sure Smart Turn must be that you have finished before it ends the segment. Lower values end more segments early, but also cut more pauses in the middle of a sentence.
settings.smartTurnMaxWaitTooltip: The longest silence before a segment ends when Smart Turn has not ended it first.
settings.smartTurnDownloading: Downloading the Smart Turn model: {{done}} of {{total}}
settings.vadMinSpeechDurationTooltip: Minimum speech duration to consider as valid speech. Filters out very short sounds like clicks or coughs.
settings.geminiVadTooltip:
Controls how Gemini detects speech pauses to split turns. Adjusting these settings can improve translation responsiveness for continuous speech. 
Push-to-Talk: hold a key to send audio. 
Push-to-Translate: like Push-to-Talk, but routes your raw mic to the virtual mic when idle so you can speak directly without translation.
settings.startOfSpeechSensitivityTooltip: How sensitive the detection is to speech starting. High sensitivity detects quieter or shorter speech onsets.
settings.endOfSpeechSensitivityTooltip: How sensitive the detection is to speech ending. High sensitivity splits turns at shorter pauses, producing more frequent translations.
settings.vadSilenceDurationTooltip: How long a silence must last before it triggers a turn split. Lower values produce faster translations but may split mid-sentence.
settings.vadPrefixPaddingTooltip: Audio padding added before detected speech. Prevents the beginning of words from being cut off.
settings.localInferenceModelsRequired: Please download the required models in <settingsLink>Settings</settingsLink> first. You need to download Speech Recognition (ASR), Translation, and Speech Synthesis (TTS) models to get started.
settings.missingModelsWarning: Missing {{types}} model(s) for this language pair.
settings.resolutionNotesSummary: {{count}} of your selected models are unavailable — automatic fallbacks are in use.
settings.resolutionNotesNamed: {{names}} unavailable — automatic fallbacks are in use.
settings.resolutionNotesNamedMore: {{names}} and {{count}} more unavailable — automatic fallbacks are in use.
settings.reasoningEffortTooltip: Controls how much the model deliberates before responding. Higher levels produce better results on complex tasks but increase latency and cost. Recommended: low for live translation. Only available for gpt-realtime-2.
settings.translateInfoBanner: This model stays silent when the speaker uses the same language as the target. Mixed-language speech may have gaps.
settings.translateModelNotAvailable: API key works, but gpt-realtime-translate is not accessible with this key.
settings.participantSectionDescriptionElectron: Translate audio from any application playing on this system.
settings.participantSectionDescriptionExtension: Translate audio from the active browser tab. The original audio plays through the default playback device you chose.
settings.edgeTtsNoVoicesForLanguage: No voices available for this language

settings.sonioxSharedSessionTooltip:
Both mode can run on one shared Soniox session or a separate session per direction.

Enabled: a single session translates both sides with automatic voice separation — lower cost and latency.

Disabled: a separate session per direction — more reliable when both people talk at once, but about twice the cost.

Only affects Both mode.
settings.sonioxSharedSessionManagedCost: Kizuna AI supports both. Disabled runs two sessions at once — about twice the cost per minute, so your session allowance runs out in about half the time and a higher balance is needed to start.
settings.sonioxSharedSessionFaceToFace: Face-to-face always uses one shared session: both people speak into the same microphone.
settings.sonioxAgentText: Use the read-aloud text to improve recognition
settings.sonioxAgentTextTooltip: Tells the recognition service what is about to be read aloud, so it recognizes replies better and leaves the read-aloud out of the transcript if your speakers reach the microphone. When speech plays on this computer, this adds a small charge.
settings.sonioxAgentTextSplitBoth: Off in two-way mode with separate sessions: there it did not keep the read-aloud out of recognition and made it harder to recognize someone talking over it. Your setting is kept.
settings.sonioxSpeakerLabelsTooltip:
Numbers the other side's people — Speaker 1, Speaker 2… — once more than one voice is heard.

It can mistake one person for several. Disabled: no numbers are shown.

Applies from the next session.
settings.voiceIHearSame: Same as the voice the other side hears, so {{voice}} reads instead.
settings.sonioxEndpointSensitivityTooltip: How readily a pause is judged as the end of an utterance — higher splits on weaker evidence (snappier, more premature cut-offs), lower demands stronger evidence. Time is bounded by the max-pause setting below. 0 is the Soniox default.
settings.sonioxEndpointMaxDelayTooltip: A hard ceiling: once speech stops, the utterance closes after at most this long, however the sensitivity judgment leans. Raise it to keep sentences with mid-sentence pauses whole; lower it for faster finalization. 2000 ms is the Soniox default.
settings.sonioxEndpointLatencyLevelTooltip: Progressively more aggressive latency reduction when closing an utterance. 0 is the default behavior.

settings.sonioxRegionTooltip: Soniox runs a separate deployment per region. Your audio is processed in the region you pick. Applies from the next session.
settings.sonioxRegionTooltipOwnKey: Soniox runs a separate deployment per region, and each one is a separate Soniox project with its own API key. Your audio is processed in the region you pick. Applies from the next session.
settings.qwenRegionTooltip: Qwen runs a separate deployment per region. Your audio is processed in the region you pick. Applies from the next session. From networks outside mainland China, Beijing may answer with noticeably higher latency.
settings.qwenRegionBeijingNote: Beijing may have noticeably higher latency from networks outside mainland China; if it does, try Singapore.
settings.sentenceSegmentationTitleDesc: Chooses where one bubble ends: leave it to the provider, cut on a pause you tune, or start a new one every few sentences with the missing punctuation added.
settings.sentenceSegmentationDesc: How a bubble is cut. Off keeps what this provider already produces. By pause cuts on a silence you tune below. By sentences adds the punctuation a transcript is missing and starts a new bubble every few sentences; it downloads three small models.
settings.sentenceSegmentationChunkTooltip: How much speech goes into one bubble before a new one starts. On local engines this is also the translation unit, so 1 translates sentence by sentence and 5 stays close to whole-utterance translation.
settings.sentenceSegmentationChunkEffect: Long speech starts a new bubble every {{count}} sentences.
settings.sentenceSegmentationChunkAutoEffect: Bubbles are cut where they are today; only the missing punctuation is added.
settings.sentenceSegmentationLowMemoryOn: This device does not report enough memory to run these models, so By sentences is not available.
settings.sentenceSegmentationDownloadBody: Sentence segmentation needs three models, one per language group. They download once and stay on this device.
settings.sentenceSegmentationDownloadMissing: The models are not on this device.

audioPanel.playsOnTip: The {{language}} translation plays here: choose the device and side (left or right) the {{language}} listener wears.
audioPanel.title: Audio Settings
audioPanel.virtualMicWarningTitle: This is a virtual microphone created by Sokuji.
audioPanel.virtualMicWarningText1: Please do not select this device here. Instead, use this virtual microphone in your video conferencing applications (like Google Meet, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, etc.) to receive the live speech translation output.
audioPanel.virtualMicWarningText2: For Sokuji to work properly, please select your actual physical microphone from the list.
audioPanel.loopbackMicWarningTitle: This input re-captures what this computer is playing.
audioPanel.loopbackMicWarningText1: Loopback inputs like "Stereo Mix" or a "Monitor of ..." device record the system's own audio output. During a session that includes Sokuji's translated speech, Sokuji would hear and translate itself in a loop.
audioPanel.loopbackMicWarningText2: The device stays selected in case this routing is intentional, but for normal use please pick a physical microphone instead.
audioPanel.passthroughManagedByPushToTranslate: In Push-to-Translate mode, passthrough is automatic — it plays at 100% volume when you're not holding the key, and stops (audio goes to translation) while you hold it.
audioPanel.speechTooltip: Which translations are spoken, to whom, and on which device.
audioPanel.defaultPlaybackTip: Sounds with no device of their own play here.
audioPanel.otherHearsTip: What I say, translated and read aloud to the other side. Into the virtual microphone: choose it as the microphone in your meeting app.
audioPanel.meTooTip: Also plays the translation the other side hears on my side (the spoken translation, not my own voice).
audioPanel.needsOtherHears: Nothing to hear while the translation is not spoken. Your setting is kept.
audioPanel.passthroughTip: Mixes my own voice, at a lower level, under the translation into the virtual microphone. 60% at most.
audioPanel.iHearTip: What the other side says, translated and read aloud to me.
audioPanel.iHearNotOffered: This service does not speak the other side's translation.
audioPanel.keepReplayTip: Keeps the spoken translations in memory so each message's ▶ works; a long session uses more memory.
audioPanel.keepReplayNothingSpoken: Nothing is spoken, so there is nothing to keep. Your setting is kept.
audioPanel.blockedWholeSystem: All system sound is being captured: these playback options are off, so the translation is not translated again.
audioPanel.lockedByMode: Not in "{{mode}}" mode. Your setting is kept.
audioPanel.rowLockedByRun: Fixed for this session; stop it to change.
audioPanel.mutualExclusivityParticipantText: Please turn off the speaker monitor before enabling Other's audio.
audioPanel.screenRecordingDeniedText1: Other's audio requires Screen Recording permission to capture system audio.
audioPanel.screenRecordingDeniedText2: Please go to System Preferences > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording and enable Sokuji.
audioPanel.screenRecordingDeniedText3: After enabling the permission, please restart the app.
audioPanel.otherSideBesideNote: The other person shares your microphone; no system audio is captured.
audioPanel.participantSourceDesc: Choose which application to translate. System Audio captures everything you hear, including games and music.
audioPanel.participantNoAudioYet: No audio has come through from the selected source yet. If it is playing and nothing is translated, allow Sokuji under System Settings > Privacy & Security > System Audio Recording Only (macOS), then start the session again.
audioPanel.audioCaptureUnprovenTitle: No audio has come through from the selected source yet
audioPanel.audioCaptureUnprovenText1: If the source is playing and nothing is translated, macOS is probably delivering silence: capturing an application needs the "System Audio Recording Only" permission, and without it there is no error, only silence.
audioPanel.screenRecordingDeniedText2Named: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording and enable "{{app}}".
audioPanel.audioCaptureDeniedText2Named: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > System Audio Recording Only and enable "{{app}}".
audioPanel.audioCaptureUnprovenText3Named: "{{app}}" only appears in that list after it has tried to capture once, which it just did. Start the session again after enabling it. If the source was simply silent, nothing needs to change.
audioPanel.screenRecordingHasAlternative: You can avoid this permission entirely: pick a specific application as Other's audio source instead. Applications only appear in that list while they are playing audio.
audioPanel.participantSourceSwitchFailed: Could not switch Other's audio source. Stop and start the session to change it.
audioPanel.participantFellBackToSystemAudio: Capture of the selected application stopped, so all system audio is being translated instead. Pick the application again to narrow it back.
audioPanel.captionTheirs: What the other side says, as speech
audioPanel.defaultPlaybackAid: Sounds on my side play here unless a row names its own device; a sound whose own device is unplugged plays here too.

simpleConfig.userAccountTooltip: For users with technical knowledge and their own API keys, you can use your own API key whether logged in or not. User Account is designed for new users who prefer a simplified setup without complex configuration.
simpleConfig.signInRequired: Sign up to use Sokuji's built-in translation service — no API key needed. You can also keep using your own provider and key.
simpleConfig.microphoneDesc: Select the microphone to capture your speech. Speak your language into this microphone, and Sokuji will translate everything it hears in real-time.

simpleConfig.textOnlyForcedByMode: "{{mode}}" mode turns what participants say into text for you and never generates audio, so Text Only stays on. Switch the translation mode to translate your own voice with speech.

qwen_livetranslate.screenContextTooltip: Lets the model see one window, tab or screen you choose, so the names and terms on it are recognized and translated as written. Everything inside that area is sent to Alibaba Cloud's Qwen service, in the region of this session, as pictures; Kizuna AI never receives them. It adds to the charge for every second of speech while it is on — on your Alibaba Cloud bill with your own key, or on your account's pricing page with a Kizuna AI account; in Both mode each direction's session is billed.

paths.ownKeyNote: Pick the provider you have an account with. Each one issues its own key:

managed.title: Start right away
managed.desc: Kizuna AI runs the translation for you.
managed.cost: Sign up with your email address and verify it — verified accounts get a trial credit. After that you top up your balance, and translation is billed by how much you use.

options.kizunaai_qwen: Can look at your screen; very accurate transcription and translation.

own-key.title: I have my own API key
own-key.desc: Bring your own key from OpenAI, Gemini, Doubao (Volcengine) and others.
own-key.cost: Your key stays on this device and reaches the provider straight from it. You are their customer: you pay them for what you use, and nothing goes through Kizuna AI.

offline.title: No key needed
offline.desc: Free. Recognition runs on this computer; translation uses Bing and speech uses Edge, which go online as Microsoft services.
offline.cost: Recognition needs a model downloaded to disk first. Runs well with a GPU; noticeably slower on CPU only.
offline.native: Native engine — faster, uses your GPU where available.

fit.cannotSpeak: This provider cannot produce spoken translation.
fit.cannotBeTextOnly: This provider always speaks; it cannot run subtitles-only.
fit.cannotFaceToFace: This provider cannot translate two people at one microphone.

credentials.onFile: A key is already saved — leave this blank to keep it.
credentials.ownKeyDesc: This key is stored on this device only, and the app calls the provider straight from here — it never reaches Kizuna AI. You pay the provider for what you use.
credentials.managedDesc: Sign up with your email address and verify it from your inbox; verified accounts get a trial credit. After that you top up your balance and pay only for what you use.
credentials.verifyEmail: Signed in. Open the link we emailed you to verify your address — the trial credit lands once you do.
credentials.offlineNotice: The recognition model is downloaded after setup, from Settings → Models and storage. Translation uses Bing and speech uses Edge: nothing to download and no account; the text to translate and the translation to speak are sent to Microsoft.
credentials.pendingKey: You can add the key later in Settings → Accounts and keys. Start stays locked until it validates.
credentials.pendingSignIn: You can sign in later from the account button. Start stays locked until then.
credentials.offlineHardware: Sokuji runs well with a GPU and enough VRAM; on CPU alone it is noticeably slower.
credentials.openaiOneKey: This one key serves OpenAI Realtime, Translate and Live.

summary.pendingKey: No API key yet — add it in Settings → Accounts and keys before you start.
summary.pendingSignIn: Not signed in — sign in from the account button before you start.

lineup.title: The line-up this sets up
lineup.later: You can change each stage later in Settings → Languages and line-up.

welcome.title: You're set up
welcome.content: Sokuji is configured for your scenario. Here is a short look around — it takes under a minute.

mode-picker.title: Translation mode
mode-picker.content: This is set for you, and you can switch it any time. The translation always appears here as text; the mode, together with the Speech block's "Translation the other side hears" switch, decides whether it is also spoken aloud.
mode-picker.modeMe: Me — what you say is translated for the other side.
mode-picker.modeOthers: Other — what they say is translated for you.

microphone.title: Your microphone
microphone.content: Your speech comes in here. The system default is already selected. Do not pick the Sokuji virtual microphone — that one is for your meeting app.

monitor.title: Hear yourself translated
monitor.content: Play the translated voice to your own headphones so you can check how it sounds. Turn it off if you do not need it.

output-routing.title: How the other side hears you
output-routing.content: Your translated voice goes to a virtual microphone; pick it as the mic in your meeting app.
output-routing.content_extension: In Google Meet, Zoom or Teams, choose "Sokuji Virtual Microphone" as your microphone. Sokuji adds it to supported meeting sites automatically.
output-routing.content_electronLinux: Sokuji created a virtual microphone on this system. Choose it as the microphone in your meeting app.
output-routing.content_electronOther: You need a virtual audio cable (for example VB-Cable). Send Sokuji's output to it, and choose it as the microphone in your meeting app.

participant-source.title: The other side's voice
participant-source.content: Sokuji listens to the other side here.
participant-source.content_electron: Choose the app to translate, or all system audio. Their original voice keeps playing as usual.
participant-source.content_extension: Sokuji translates the audio of the current tab. Their original voice keeps playing as usual.

subtitle.title: Subtitle mode
subtitle.content_electron: Shrinks this window into a floating subtitle bar that OBS and screen sharing can capture. “Return to main window” on the bar, or Esc, brings the window back.
subtitle.content_extension: Opens floating subtitles as an overlay on the page. OBS and screen sharing can capture it.

account.title: Your account
account.content: Your balance and top-up live here.
account.content_signedOut: Your account lives here. Sign in after the tour to unlock Start.

provider-settings.title: Provider settings
provider-settings.content_pending: Paste your API key here. Start unlocks once it validates.

models.title: Models
models.content: Download models here — one per stage. Try a few; the first pick is not the only good one.

start.title: Start
start.content: Press here to start translating. If the button stays greyed out, hover it: the note names what is still missing and where to put it right.
start.content_offline: This lights up once your models are ready. Hover it while it is grey to see what it is waiting for.
start.content_signedOut: This lights up once you sign in. Hover it while it is grey to see what it is waiting for.
start.content_pendingKey: This lights up once your API key validates. Hover it while it is grey to see what it is waiting for.

done.title: That's it
done.content: Everything else is in Settings, one category at a time; search finds any setting by name. Replay this guide any time from Help.

vbCable.body: Meeting apps take the spoken translation through a virtual microphone. On Windows that is VB-CABLE, a free driver from VB-Audio. Everything else in Sokuji works without it.

vbCable.storeStep3: Click "Install Driver", then restart your PC.

intro.accounts: Accounts and keys: each service is filled in once. Once it is, what it can do is chosen in "Languages and line-up".
intro.models: Every model downloaded to this computer is managed here: the ones sessions use, the helpers, and imported voices.
intro.audio: Microphone, speech and the other side's audio. Everything except "Translation the other side hears" can be changed during a session.
intro.display: The same values as the buttons above the conversation and on the caption bar: change them on either side, and they apply at once. The main window and caption mode each keep their own.

audio.otherHint: Where the other side's voice comes in

flow.caption: Where the sound goes. Lit lines are on now, dashed ones off; they follow the switches below.
flow.ariaSteps: Where the sound goes: what I say is translated, then made into speech that goes into the virtual microphone for the other side, and plays on my side too when I hear it; what the other side says is translated, then made into speech that plays on my playback device. With a speech switch off, the translation is made but not spoken.

wordList.byModelNote: Depends on model: OpenAI takes the background with its older transcription models only; Gemini Live takes the terms with gemini-3.8-live only; this device reads the list with its large language model translators only.
